speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks swollen. To understand what is wrong, can you tell me if you are passing stool or gas, and have you had any episodes of crying with your legs pulled up to your chest?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

Based on the clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, fussiness, and pain exacerbated by palpation, the findings are highly suggestive of intussusception. Immediate surgical consultation is required.
